summary: Tenant-scoped service principal role mapping fails due to trailing whitespace and case mismatch in SCIM group names
description:
Issue summary:
Customer uses tenant-scoped Azure AD service principals to run scheduled inference jobs inside their private deployment. After a recent SCIM sync, calls authenticated with the service principal intermittently receive 403 Forbidden from the Redwood Private endpoint. The customer reports the behavior started after provisioning a new role binding via their IdP provisioning (SCIM).

Impact:
- Several scheduled batch jobs that use the tenant-scoped SP to call the /api/v1/infer endpoint fail ~30% of the time with 403s.
- Real user-facing tasks are delayed; customer flags this as blocking their production SLA for nightly reconciliation.

Environment:
- Private deployment (on-prem) behind customer-managed edge router.
- Private control plane with KMS integration.
- Region: us-east.
- IdP: Azure AD automatic provisioning (SCIM v2).

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Create a tenant-scoped service principal in Azure AD and assign it to SCIM-provisioned group "beacon-inference-ops" (note: provisioning UI showed displayName as "beacon-inference-ops ").
2) Ensure the SCIM sync runs and verify the group is present in Redwood Console -> Settings -> Role mappings.
3) Trigger a scheduled inference job using the SP credentials (JWT client credentials flow).
4) Observe intermittent 403 responses with X-Request-ID and auth rejection in logs.

Observed logs (redacted):
- auth-proxy.log: 2026-03-09T22:04:12Z WARN auth: mapping lookup failed for principal=sp://beacon-sp-01 group="beacon-inference-ops" reason="no_exact_match" request_id=abc123
- gateway.log: 2026-03-09T22:04:12Z ERROR request: response=403 message="forbidden: missing role binding" request_id=abc123

Notes from customer: "We see the group in the console but some of the jobs succeed and others fail; when failures happen they always have a mapping lookup failure in auth-proxy logs. We suspect provisioning normalized the name differently than how Redwood stores it."
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Initial triage – collected request IDs and asked customer for SCIM provisioning snapshot and a failing JWT sample.

2026-03-10 11:47 - Diego Martinez (Auth Eng): Reproduced locally by creating a group with trailing space in SCIM payload. Auth lookup code compares raw displayName and is failing to normalize whitespace/case. Filing hypothesis to validate in staging.

2026-03-11 08:03 - Customer (Beacon SRE - Maria Chen): Provided SCIM logs and export showing group displayName was created as "beacon-inference-ops " (trailing space) via an on-prem sync rule. Confirmed that removing trailing space in Azure fixed the issue for newly provisioned SPs but older mappings remained inconsistent.

2026-03-11 13:20 - Diego Martinez (Auth Eng): Deployed a staging patch that trims whitespace and lowercases group names during SCIM upsert and role-mapping lookup. Ran smoke tests against private staging and observed stable mappings across 1000 simulated requests.

2026-03-12 10:05 - SRE (Kenji Ito): Ran rolling restart of auth-proxy on customer staging node; no increased error rate post-restart. Preparing recommended remediation steps for customer prod rollout.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: SCIM provisioning from customer's IdP created groups with inconsistent normalization (trailing whitespace and mixed case). Current SCIM upsert and RBAC matching are performing exact string matches against stored displayName, causing intermittent 403s when SP tokens reference the variant without whitespace. Verified locally by repro: creating group with trailing space leads to no_exact_match. Patch: normalize displayName by trimming whitespace and lowercasing both during SCIM ingestion and RBAC lookup. Also identified a data-migration gap: existing tenant records may contain legacy variants and require a normalization pass. Related code: auth-proxy/group_upsert.go and rbac/matcher.go.
resolution_notes: Workaround provided to customer: (1) Remove trailing whitespace from group displayName in Azure AD and re-trigger SCIM full sync; (2) Re-provision affected service principals. Permanent fix: deployed staging patch to trunk that normalizes group names on ingestion and lookup; PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-provisioner/pull/678 merges normalization and a migration script. Will schedule a minor release v1.4.2 to roll to private customers next week. Follow-ups: run a one-time normalization migration on customer tenant data (coordinated with customer due to audit concerns) and add regression tests for SCIM name variants.
